status: Extension session-pin resume, inherited child pins, branch/reload replay, live-provider handoff and composed-registry lifting verified against the unchanged upstream extension; native session-journal transport and the /switch-account command itself remain outside this lane

upstreamSpecCases.tests/extension-resume.spec.ts: 8 declarations; 5 mapped to resume scenarios, 2 to composition scenarios, 1 (stale session ctx) deferred to the lift/context evidence
upstreamSpecCases.tests/extension-composition.spec.ts: 2 declarations; both mapped to composition scenarios
upstreamSpecCases.tests/session-pins.spec.ts: 9 declarations; parsing/inherited-env/replay already covered by scheduler-evidence, extension-level composition covered here
upstreamSpecCases.tests/extension-failover.spec.ts: covered by the retry/Fabric lane, not duplicated

compared: Resume replay: the journal's latest decision per pool and key, applied to a fresh scheduler
An explicit return to automatic replays as `clear`, and the follower sees the account drop to null
A removed or disabled pinned account warns with the exact upstream message and falls back to automatic
Inherited env pins rebound onto the child session's affinity key and journalled with that key
The child journal wins over inherited env pins for the same pool
A stale inherited pin warns and is not journalled
An inherited pin stays pending until its pool registers, then applies at the next reconcile
Branch prefixes (a journal cut between decisions) and reloads (shutdown then start) replay the decision that is current then
Reload does not re-journal an inherited pin because the replayed entry now decides the pool
Explicit pins outrank a pool with affinity disabled
The complete `{journal, notifications, accountChanges, active}` effect of every resume case
Every registerProvider/unregisterProvider with the registered provider's classification (lift, lifted base, shared headers) and the registry left behind, for plain and Pi-composed registries
One lift per session from the real base, never another session's lift or Pi's composed copy of it
Sessions hand the registry back to the newest live lift in whatever order they end; the last one restores the base
A departing subagent leaves the parent's virtual provider registered; the last session unregisters it
Virtual template healing re-registers a config exactly once, when the backing provider first resolves
realBase through a composed wrapper and through a lift of a lift; isLiftOf identity guards; replaceLiveProvider with an absent previous provider
install warns once and stays uninstalled while the base provider is missing, then lifts it when the base appears
limits: The reference boots a new extension instance against a fresh scheduler in the same process; it does not reopen a session file on disk or start a second OS process.

`ctx.sessionManager.getEntries` and `pi.appendEntry` are host callbacks in the port; Pi's session-file write, branch formation and tree navigation are not exercised. The resume module consumes the entries a real extension instance produced.
The live `/switch-account` command that writes the journal belongs to the commands lane; this lane replays genuine journals it produced rather than re-implementing the picker.

`extension-resume.spec.ts`'s stale-context case (a lifted provider kept usable after its session ctx is disposed) is a fresh-runtime/context-ownership concern covered by the lift evidence, not by this lane.

The prose `request` in the composition scenarios resolves through Pi's composed wrapper. The reference asserts the base credential (`k-default`) serves, matching the spec's claim that a second lift would surface the stored account instead; the port compares the provider graph decisions, not credential bytes.
Extension failover ordering versus the lift state machine (`extension-failover.spec.ts`) is verified by the retry/Fabric lane's differential evidence and is deliberately not duplicated here.
Virtual configs are supplied from the reference's store snapshot; store persistence and permissions are covered by the store evidence.
